episode_title: Go-to-Market and AI Success with Emin Can Turan from Pebbles Ai

real_qa.q: What does GTM (Go-to-Market) encompass in a B2B company?
real_qa.r: GTM is the widest terminology that encapsulates marketing strategy, marketing execution, market intelligence, social media marketing, sales, and even product rollout. It is the entire journey from the moment a person is touched somewhere without a name or email all the way through to becoming a customer and receiving ongoing service. It represents how you arrange your organizational structure, revenue function, and customer experience as a whole.
real_qa.requete: what does GTM go-to-market mean definition

real_qa.q: Why is founder energy important in a go-to-market system?
real_qa.r: Founders typically serve three roles: innovator and visionary, and salesperson. Customers want to see the founder, especially at the bottom of the funnel in the beginning. However, as companies grow, founders are pushed further down the pyramid. Energy is critical because with an inefficient GTM approach, founders waste effort and time on wrong channels and value propositions. A finite amount of dopamine and enthusiasm drives sales performance—if you do eight high-intensity calls in a day, you can barely get out of your chair because you have left it all on the call.

real_qa.q: How should persuasion science frameworks like ethos-pathos-logos be applied across a B2B marketing funnel?
real_qa.r: Six persuasion science frameworks have been mapped across the funnel, with specific applications at each stage. At the top of the funnel, push credibility first through social proof like five-star reviews on Clutch or Google and net promoter scores to establish ethos. Then move to pathos by telling a story about why you are reaching out and showing empathy for founder challenges. Finally, introduce logos—the logic of terms—with offers like a fully free trial if they like it. Each stage should leverage different sciences based on how the mind works.
real_qa.requete: ethos pathos logos marketing funnel persuasion science

real_qa.q: What does Hofstede's Culture Matrix reveal about go-to-market strategy across different markets?
real_qa.r: Hofstede's Culture Matrix maps clusters of values across individualism versus collectivism. The Dutch, Australians, New Zealand, UK, and America are clustered together, indicating that a successful product or service story in America can more easily be adapted to the UK or Netherlands without major changes. However, it is much harder to take a successful American product or service to the Middle East or Far East countries. You cannot assume that having a few clients in one country means you can simply replicate success in another—it might just be your personal network.

real_qa.q: Why do nine out of ten companies fail according to go-to-market analysis?
real_qa.r: Most company failures can be attributed to go-to-market reasons: subpar market intelligence (targeting declining or shrinking markets), wrong pricing strategy, or incorrect value propositions and ICPs for personas. These are mathematical variables—if you get one wrong, you will miss. Additionally, 70 percent of mid-sized companies do not hit their sales targets according to Salesforce, and enterprise companies take six months to two years just for a pilot rollout due to technical, legal, and commercial due diligence.

real_qa.q: What special early adopter pricing does Pebbles AI offer to its first users?
real_qa.r: The first 10,000 users will receive the same pricing for an entire year and priority access to all features and latest technology. The pricing will eventually be quadrupled, but early adopters lock in at the current rate, which is described as cents on the dollar compared to what the full price will be.
